title: Causal Effect Identification in Alternative Acyclic Directed Mixed Graphs with Residual Substitution
banked_reason: D0.5 graded incremental below the field floor: the promised positive aADMG forest completeness converse remains open and soundness/ValLoc obligations remain unrepaired.
gap_reasons: The promised sound-complete arbitrary-query procedure has been replaced by a sound rule plus examples and an expressly open forest converse; reframe the contribution around the delivered sound calculus or prove the stated completeness object.

ForestHandle merely records leaf deletions and semialgebraic calls: it neither proves that every saturated state reaches a varying fiber nor constructs the proposed positive non-Gaussian twins when Gaussian fibers are constant.
The load-bearing magnified-separation proof also substitutes an informal constraint-elimination argument for a precise deterministic-LWF factorization or cited global-Markov theorem.
proof_attempt_summary: D-0.5 accepted a field-tier proposal; D0 constructed a residual-recovery calculus, a four-node case outside the published component test, and an exact positive Gaussian nonidentification fiber. D0.5 found that the promised arbitrary-query completeness converse remained open; the recovered-state invariant, deterministic-LWF factorization, and location-oracle framing also need repair. The achieved tier was incremental, below the field floor, so formalization did not begin.
tldr: Under the maintained pointwise-positive disturbance-density class, positive real aADMGs contain observational information that Peña's component calculus does not retain: a conditionally identified mechanism yields a residual that can unlock another mechanism. RAID is a total finite automaton: it exhausts a candidate vertex, validates the observable location class, substitutes a residual only on the unique branch, returns the terminal intervention pushforward, returns a saturated state, or returns a typed empty or nonunique location record. A complete four-node trace lists every candidate and all three unique validations, while an explicit component and ancestry calculation shows why the published test fails. An exact rational Gaussian fiber supplies a positive same-law unequal-effect forest witness. The open kernel asks whether every error-forest failure admits a length-\(n\) leaf certificate of this form.
gap: Peña (2017), Table 3 and Theorems 8--9, gives a sound arbitrary-query component algorithm and a singleton completeness result in a broader disturbance class; Peña (2018) explicitly leaves arbitrary-query completeness open. Peña and Bendtsen (2017), Theorem 12 and pages 19--20, obtain necessity by copying disturbances, which is excluded by the pointwise positive density condition, and their singleton intervention with all remaining variables as outcome does not cover the \(G_4\) sub-outcome residual functional.
fill: The paper supplies the magnified graph, complete six-transition RAID syntax with typed location-validation exits, exact observational-kernel composition, finite state and oracle bounds, and a worked four-node strict separation with all eight downstream candidates, all three validations, and the published algorithm's component and ancestry failure record. A rational three-node covariance has an exactly parameterized positive Gaussian fiber with two unequal-effect points. Completeness remains an error-forest question whose leaf certificate calls a specified semialgebraic fiber decision at most once per leaf; no completeness or polynomial algebraic-runtime claim is made.
